about: The evangelium of the formulary “11th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus left the region of Tyre and came by way of Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis. And to Him they bring a man deaf and mute, and they kept begging Him to place His hand upon him. And taking him apart from the crowd, He placed His fingers in his ears; and He spat and touched his tongue; and He looked up to heaven and sighed, and said to him: Ephphetha, which is, Be opened. And at once his ears were opened, and the fetter of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking correctly. And He charged them not to tell anyone. But the more He charged them, so much the more they made it known; and they were all the more amazed, saying: He has done all things well, and He has made the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.
